title: Simple to use, pretty, and the data is yours
body:
I've previously used – or in fact not used – another, much more comprehensive, app.  I switched to HabitKit as a fresh start.  Here's why it's great:

It's simple, without masses of bells and whistles.  That means I actually get stuff done rather than fiddling with it endlessly.  I hope it always stays simple.

It's really pretty.  You *want* to use it.  That's a huge advantage!

It's not based around some opaque cloudy AI nonsense: your data is yours and you can export it in comprehensible JSON which you could easily massage in other programs and then import again.  That's a huge win for me.

It has the usual subscription thing.  But there's a lifetime option: work out how many hours you need to get back to pay for that and it is not many.

It's great.

Here are three improvements I would like:

Multi-step habits should have options to name the step (so 'minutes doing x' say) and should be weighted so completing, say, 60 minutes counts as one completion (I've asked the author about this: he's very responsive).

It would be nice if it had a feature to automagically dump the JSON data to a file once a day or so.

It would be nice if the JSON format was documented (it might be, I haven't checked this in fact).

title: Clear Concise Habit Tracking
body: This is exactly what I was looking for in a habit tracking app. The majority of other apps are too busy, I wanted something streamlined that could show me the days I’d achieved my habits at a glance - this does exactly that and it looks awesome. I also love that you can back-fill habits you’ve completed before getting the app. My only criticism is that it took me a few minutes to figure out the structure of the squares for habits completed - it was irritating me at first that there seemed to be no order. But I quickly realised they resemble days of the year, divided into 52 rows for weeks, Monday-Sunday from top to bottom. Some initial guidance on setup would be fab (apologies if this is already in place and I missed it!). Otherwise, easily the best habit tracking app for anyone who loves things simple, streamlined, and visually pleasing.
